newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore PAP takes 29 of first 31 seats announced.
newsitem.headline: Singapore PAP takes 29 of first 31 seats announced.

text.p: Singapore's ruling People's Action Party took 29 of the first 31 seats for which results were announced in Singapore's Thursday general election.

Returns from a key five-member constituency were still to be announced. Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong had pronounced that race the most important in the election and staked his prestige on the PAP winning there.
The PAP had already taken 47 seats in the 83-member parliament on Nomination Day December 23, when the opposition failed to contest them.
The Singapore Democratic Party (SDP), which held three seats in the last parliament, has been shut out of the next one. Two SDP incumbents lost and a third switched to another opposition party.
SDP leader Chee Soon Juan, one of the opposition's most prominent figures, was among those losing his bid for parliament.
A five-man Workers' Party slate faced the PAP in the winner-take-all Cheng San constituency, where counting was continuing.
